questions: Q1: Do the CLI handlers correctly follow existing patterns and send requests to the right server endpoints?
Q2: Does the manifest default env reading work correctly for both handlers?

answers.answer: Yes. Both cmdNetsuite and cmdRun follow the resolveRepo -> hxFetch POST -> console.log JSON pattern from db.ts and logs.ts. cmdNetsuite POSTs to /{repoId}/netsuite with {type, query/scriptId, env}. cmdRun POSTs to /{repoId}/run with {code, modules?, env?}. Both use configOrHelp for auth loading and proper flag parsing via getFlag/getPositionalArgs.
evidence: src/inspect/db.ts pattern comparison — identical resolveRepo -> hxFetch -> console.log flow

answers.answer: Yes. Both handlers share the same readManifestDefaultEnv pattern: read /tmp/helix-inspect/manifest.json, parse JSON, check for nsDefaultEnv string field, map PRODUCTION to 'prod' and SANDBOX to 'sandbox'. The --env flag overrides the manifest default when provided. Falls back gracefully (returns undefined) when the manifest is unavailable.

statement: Code review completed for helix-cli. No issues found. All 4 files (2 new handlers, 2 modified routers) correctly implement the CLI surface for BLD-693. Both handlers follow existing patterns, send requests to correct server endpoints, and support --env with manifest default fallback. TypeScript typecheck passes.
